# Copilot instructions

## Build and test

- Build the solution: `dotnet build Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.slnx`
- Run the test suite: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj`
- Run one test: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~WorkItemServiceTests.Accept_Hierarchy_CreatesLabelledSubIssuesAndOnlyAssignsTheStory"`
- Restore the local EF tool before using it: `dotnet tool restore`
- Set `ConnectionStrings__Database` in the shell before using EF tools (use the connection string from your local development settings).
- Add a migration: `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql --output-dir Migrations`
- Check the migration snapshot: `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql`
- Azure deployment: `.github\workflows\release.yml` builds and tests on pushes and pull requests to `main`. On every push to `main`, it applies an EF migrations bundle to Azure SQL and deploys to App Service. One-time OIDC setup is in `scripts\setup-azure-github.ps1`; see `docs\azure-deployment.md`.

The app targets .NET 10. Development startup applies EF migrations automatically and uses the LocalDB connection string in `appsettings.Development.json`; other environments must supply `ConnectionStrings:Database`. `appsettings.Development.json` is gitignored and holds personal settings such as `OpenAI:ApiKey`; create it by copying the tracked `appsettings.Development.example.json` (keep the template free of secrets and in sync when adding settings). Neither file is published.

## Architecture

- Project references flow from `Web` to `Application`, and from `Application` to `DataAccess.Sql` and `Agents`. All libraries share `Contracts`, which has no application or infrastructure dependencies. Keep Web free of EF and Agent Framework types.
- `Application/Features` contains MediatR commands, queries, handlers and FluentValidation validators grouped by feature, one type per file in `Commands`, `Queries` and `Validators` subfolders (e.g. `WorkItems/Queries/GetWorkItemQuery.cs` and `GetWorkItemQueryHandler.cs`); these keep the feature namespace. Requests and responses wrap records from `Contracts`; collection responses wrap `CollectionResult<T>`. UI-facing application services dispatch through MediatR, whose validation pipeline runs before handlers.
- `DataAccess.Sql` owns EF entities, DTO mapping, stores, `AppDbContext`, migrations and the design-time factory. Stores live in `Stores` behind interfaces (`IWorkItemStore`, ...) that are registered and injected through DI. Entity configuration lives in `Configuration`, one `ModelBuilder` extension per entity, called from `OnModelCreating`. Stores use `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>` and dispose a context per operation. DTOs are separate records, not EF entities. Existing migration IDs and the database schema are preserved.
- `Agents` owns Microsoft Agent Framework agents, sessions, streaming and AI form tools. `Application.Features.Assistant` exposes framework-free conversations and tool factories to Web. Contract records are mutable where form binding requires it; use `Copy()` or `with` for editable copies.
- This is a .NET 10 Blazor app using Interactive Server rendering without prerendering for interactive routes. GitHub OAuth is single-user: `Program.cs` enforces the configured allowed login and keeps the access token in the server-side authentication ticket. GitHub API calls get the token from the `GitHubClaims.AccessToken` claim through `AuthenticationStateProvider`.
- The app operates on one selected repository per Blazor circuit. `RepositoryContext` restores and stores the selection in protected browser local storage; `MainLayout` requires a selection and keys the page body by repository full name so switching repositories recreates the page. Pages marked `[RepositoryIndependent]` (detected through the `RouteData` cascaded from `Routes.razor`) render without a selection, e.g. the agent template pages.
- Repository selection and restored selections update SQL `RepositoryAccesses` through `RepositoryHistoryService`. The picker loads the five most recent names/access times independently of GitHub's full repository list and fetches a recent repository directly when selected before that list finishes.
- Agent templates (`AgentTemplateService`) are stored in SQL Server as full agent file content, are shared across repositories, and are applied to one or more repositories through the application workflow and `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentEditor` and `AgentTemplateEditor` share the `Components/Shared/AgentForm.razor` form.
- Repository-backed features should use `RepositoryContext.Current` and pass the repository full name through application service operations. Work items are scoped by repository; the managed AI model catalog, agent templates and work item templates are shared across repositories.
- Work items (epics, features, user stories, bugs and tasks) share one model: `WorkItem` with a `WorkItemType`, stored in the `WorkItems` table with a self-referencing `ParentId`; templates are `WorkItemTemplate` rows per type. `WorkItemTypeRules` (Contracts) holds the label, label color, names and hierarchy per type: a feature needs an epic parent, a story needs a feature parent, bugs and tasks are standalone or part of an epic, feature or story. Only stories, bugs and tasks are assigned to the Copilot cloud agent; the store clears assignment settings for epics and features. `WorkItemStore` enforces the hierarchy and refuses to delete items with children. `WorkItemWorkflow` creates the labelled issue (creating the label when missing), makes it a sub-issue of the parent's issue and makes the issues of already accepted children its sub-issues (the sub-issues API needs GitHub's issue id, stored as `IssueId`).
- The work item pages (`WorkItems`, `WorkItemEditor`, `WorkItemTemplates`, `WorkItemTemplateEditor`) each serve all types through one `@page` per type; `WorkItemRoutes` maps types to URLs (`/epics`, `/features`, `/stories`, `/bugs`, `/tasks`, `/{label}-templates`) and reads the type from the URL. The pages take the cascaded `RouteData` so navigating between types (same component) reloads them.
- Custom agent profiles live in each repository's `.github/agents` directory and are read or committed through `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentFileSerializer` preserves unedited YAML frontmatter keys and their order; retain that behavior when changing agent-file editing.
- DGHSF's internal agents use the singleton `AssistantAgentFactory` in `Agents` and the `OpenAI` config section (`Endpoint`, `Model`, `ApiKey`; unconfigured means the chat shows a setup hint). The fixed set of agents and their default system prompts live in `InternalAgentDefaults` (keys in Contracts `InternalAgentKeys`): one Copilot per work item type, per work item template type, for agents and for agent templates, plus the background agents Model Selector and Chat Suggestions. They are stored in the `InternalAgents` table (seeded at startup through `SeedApplicationDataAsync` and whenever the list is loaded; seeding adds missing agents and refreshes name/description but keeps edited prompts and the enabled flag). `InternalAgentRegistry` merges the stored prompt with the defaults; `/internal-agents` edits the prompt, enables/disables and resets an agent. Internal agents are global, not per repository.
- Copilot chats: Web uses `AssistantChat` with a `CopilotKey` and tools from `AssistantForms.ForAgent` / `ForWorkItem` / `ForWorkItemTemplate`. Form tools read and update state through an `onUi` callback (`InvokeAsync` + `StateHasChanged`) and expose a form snapshot. Tools only change the form; the user saves. A disabled Copilot hides its chat. Before a conversation starts, `AssistantChat` asks the Chat Suggestions agent (`BackgroundAgents.SuggestPromptsAsync`, with the form snapshot) for 3 chips; the page's static suggestions are the fallback. On the work item editors the chips are written again (`AssistantChat.RefreshSuggestions`) when the title or description loses focus after a change (`MarkdownEditor.OnBlur`), not per keystroke; during a conversation no chips are shown, so nothing is refreshed.
- Background agents (`BackgroundAgents`) use structured output (`RunAsync<T>`), so edited prompts can't break the result format. `WorkItemModelSelector` lets the Model Selector suggest an enabled managed model for a story, bug or task (`WorkItemService.SelectModelAsync`; nothing is saved). The work item editor debounces it: 3 seconds after the last description change (typed or filled in by the Copilot) it shows the suggestion as a chip under the model picker, and clicking the chip applies it. It also suggests once, without delay, when an existing draft with a description is opened; other fields and new items (template skeletons) don't trigger it. The model is never picked automatically: "Auto" stays Copilot's automatic model selection.
- `MarkdownEditor` (Toast UI) replaces Toast UI's base64 image hook through `MarkdownEditor.razor.js`, installed on the ToastUIEditor package's private `_instance` interop object (guarded by `ImageUploadTests`). With `AllowImages` (work item and work item template editors) and the `ImageUploads` config section set, images stream over the circuit to `ImageUploadService`, which validates the format by signature and stores them under a random name in a public Azure blob container (`IImageStorage`); otherwise images are refused.
- Write extension methods with C# 14 `extension(...)` blocks.
- Use block bodies (`{ ... }`) for methods, constructors, operators and local functions, also in Razor `@code` blocks; expression bodies only where a block is not possible. `.editorconfig` enforces this for C# files.
- UI pages are Razor components using MudBlazor. Tests use xUnit and bUnit in `tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests`.

## Repository guidance

`README.md` is only a brief project description. `IDEAS.md` includes both implemented features and roadmap items; confirm behavior in the source before treating planned features as available.
